doc_name: Figure skating at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Ice dance
text: The ice dance competition in figure skating at the 2022 Winter Olympics took place on 12 February (rhythm dance) and 14 February (free dance) at the Capital Indoor Stadium in Haidian District, Beijing. Gabriella Papadakis and Guillaume Cizeron of France won the event, with Victoria Sinitsina and Nikita Katsalapov, representing the Russian Olympic Committee, securing silver, and Madison Hubbell and Zachary Donohue of the United States earning bronze. The 2018 champions Tessa Virtue and Scott Moir, along with bronze medalists Maia Shibutani and Alex Shibutani, retired from competition. Papadakis and Cizeron achieved the highest score of the 2021–22 season prior to the Olympics, while Sinitsina and Katsalapov recorded the second-highest score of the season and are the 2021 World champions, during which Papadakis/Cizeron did not compete. In ice dance, major errors are rare, and Olympic scores generally align with those from the season, making Papadakis/Cizeron and Sinitsina/Katsalapov the top contenders, with Papadakis/Cizeron as the favorites. During the rhythm dance, Papadakis and Cizeron broke their own world record to gain a two-point lead over Sinitsina and Katsalapov, which they then extended by winning the free dance by five points, narrowly missing their own world record. Their combined total score set a new world record, and they claimed gold by 6.5 points over Sinitsina/Katsalapov. Hubbell and Donohue finished third in both segments to win bronze by four points ahead of their American teammates Madison Chock and Evan Bates. Before the competition, the existing ISU best scores were recorded, and the following new best scores were established during the event. The rhythm dance was held on 12 February, the free dance on 14 February, and skaters were ranked based on their total combined (overall) score.
